exercise.name: Barbell Bent Over Wide Grip Row

reference.title: Barbell Bent Over Wide Grip Row
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Brace in the hinge, breathe out as the bar comes up, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: lighter than a close-grip row; the trunk stays still, about 2 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches the lower chest without the trunk rising.

cues.text: Overhand grip well outside the shoulders, knees soft, hinge until the trunk is about 30-40 degrees above the floor, back flat, arms long.
Lead with the elbows out to the sides and pull the bar to the lower chest.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for a moment; the trunk stays still.
Lower the bar slowly to straight arms.
Keep the hinge and the brace; start the next rep without standing up.

mistakes.mistake: Standing up and heaving the bar
mistakes.fix: Fix the trunk angle; lighten the load until it stays still.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder blades back and down, not up.
With the wide grip, aim for the lower chest with the elbows out at about 60-75 degrees from the trunk.
Chest proud, brace, hinge only as far as a flat back allows.

kinematics.norm: Bent-over rows load the lumbar spine and extensors; the trunk is held still (Fenwick 2009); about 30-45 degrees above horizontal is common
Wide grip with flared elbows shifts work toward the rear deltoid and mid back (Schoenfeld 2013 on hand position and posterior shoulder EMG)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Hold the brace and the hinge for the whole set; set the bar down if the back starts to round.
Low-back pain: use a chest-supported row instead.
Shoulder pain with the flared elbows: narrow the grip and bring the elbows in.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower back tires: more upright trunk or chest-supported row.
regressions: Seated cable row with a wide bar.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: The wide grip and flared elbows put the rear shoulders to work (horizontal abduction).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Extends the shoulder; less than in a close, elbows-in row.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Extends the shoulder; less than in a close, elbows-in row.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbows; the overhand grip keeps it a helper.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbows; the overhand grip keeps it a helper.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Holds the upper arm turned out as the elbows flare.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder blades; do not shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder blades; do not shrug.
